pr_title: Allow Protected Branches to Whitelist Deploy Keys
pr_body: Fix #8472 Add option to allow protected branches to whitelist writing deploy keys.
pr_comments: This does slightly change current practice - so that if people currently rely on the fact that the deploy key is the owner of the repo and have whitelisted the owner, then that won't work anymore and they'll have to whitelist the deploy key,

issue_context.title: How to allow push from server to repo on protected branch?
issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref):
- Git version: 2.17.1
- Operating system: Ubuntu 18.04
- Database (use `[x]`):
  - [x] PostgreSQL
  - [ ] MySQL
  - [ ] MSSQL
  - [ ] SQLite
- Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io:
  - [x] Yes (provide example URL)
  - [ ] No
  - [ ] Not relevant
- Log gist:

So I am using a deployment service (Laravel Forge) and I want to automatically push production updates back to a protected branch before I deploy new updates. I am encountering this issue though and I'm not sure what the recommended approach would be. I had this working fine in Gitlab with a protect branch and the same SSH deploy key. (write access is enabled in Gitea for this branch.)

```
remote: Gitea: protected branch master can not be pushed to
```

What is the recommend approach with Gitea for pushing updates from production back to the repo on a protected brach?
comments:
You could add a whitelist.

Deploy keys act as the repository owner so if you add the repository owner to the whitelist that should work.

(Now, that might be difficult with an organisation but let me think)

We could add another option to the protection to allow writing deploy keys to push.

I solved this by adding my individual key (as organization and repository owner) to the server and setting `.ssh/config` to use that key when pushing back to the Gitea server.

The additional option sounds like a great idea though @zeripath. This would enable more fine grained control.

review_comments: As this comes from the environment, there's a risk it's spoofed. This value should be calculated in-process from the key itself.

Apologies if I'm misunderstanding your comment - but I'll quickly run through how git and git hook work:

* Say you do a `git push` to any SSH git server. Once it is ready, `git` will effectively send `ssh git@giteaserver "git receive-pack :username/:reponame"` - the actual data will be sent over stdin / stdout for that connection.
* Now assuming you're logging in with a key, ssh will match your key with a line in authorized_keys (or it uses an AuthorizedKeys command to generate the line.)
* In Gitea's case this will match something like: 
```
command="/home/git/gitea/gitea serv key-2 --config='/home/git/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini'",no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding,no-agent-forwarding,no-pty ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nz... user@something
```
* When SSH sees the `command="..."` it immediately runs that command and stores a copy of the command that it was told to run in `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`
* Note that `key-2` - SSH *never* exposes the key to command or to SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND if it runs.
  * In the case of the internal SSH it's basically the same.
* `gitea serv` needs to ensure that `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND` is one of the acceptable commands so if it's not it will stop there.
* `gitea serv` will check if the key argument provided should have access to the repository at all - but because it doesn't know what you're sending it cannot assess if you're trying to access a protected branch - it also cannot know if the commit fails. It therefore interprets the key-2 and expands it to a set of environment variables see: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/f9aba9ba0f07b77cb46dde6eda3c3f5b8fa841fe/cmd/serv.go#L187-L193
  * `gitea serv` is, now, mostly a lightweight shim that does almost of all its work by sending a request to `/private/serv/command/:keyid/:owner/:repo` - however it does need to know where gitea is etc. hence the `--config`.
  * It's also worth noting that we're running `gitea serv` here as a new process - in a possibly completely separate environment to that which starts the `gitea web` process hence my comments on environment-to-ini PR - it can only configure by the ini - so the ini has to be correct.
* Once it's set the environment variables it will then exec the correct git command.
* It is the git commands, within its environment, that will then call the hooks that are stored in the git repository e.g. `.git/hooks/pre-receive.d/gitea`. So environment variables are the only way to configure this.
  * It's only during pre-receive that you can actually work out if you're touching a protected branch.
  * The calling of hooks explains why if people change their gitea command name they have to re-synchronize hooks - (there is another solution to this I've spoken about before.)

Unless you want to rewrite git entirely you only have environment variables but you do have control over these.
I'm sorry, as I was looking at the small diff window I got confused with cmd serv, where we do check those things. My apologies.
